The pressure at section 30 is calculated using the telescoping form of the Bernoulli equation with losses. Summing the kinetic energy change, gravitational potential energy change, and frictional losses from section 1 to 30 yields:

\[
p_{30} = p_1 + \frac{1}{2}\rho (v_1^2 - v_{30}^2) + \rho g (z_1 - z_{30}) - \frac{1}{2}\rho \sum_{i=1}^{29} K_i v_i^2.
\]

Given \(p_1 = 278\ \text{kPa}\), \(\rho = 1000\ \text{kg/m}^3\), \(g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2\), \(Q = 22\ \text{L/s} = 0.022\ \text{m}^3/\text{s}\), and areas in \(\text{cm}^2\) converted to \(\text{m}^2\) via \(v_i = 220/A_i\) (with \(A_i\) in \(\text{cm}^2\)), the computation gives:

\[
p_{30} = 187.121\ \text{kPa} \approx 187.1\ \text{kPa}
\]

to four significant figures.

ANSWER: 187.1
